votes.question: Booker Amdt. No. 6835 — To establish certain standards with respect to coaches of varsity sports teams.
votes.plain_language: This amendment would have let coaches move between four-year colleges under transfer rules like those for athletes, and it would have voided a coach's endorsement deal unless the pay matched similar non-coaches and had a real business purpose. A Yea would have added those rules. A Nay rejected them.

votes.question: Booker Amdt. No. 6805 — To increase the limitation on funding for post-eligibility insurance and catastrophic injury for student athletes.
votes.plain_language: This amendment would have capped a student-athlete insurance and catastrophic-injury fund at $200 million and required major conferences and an athletic association to cover any amount above $100 million. A Yea would have set that cap. A Nay rejected it.

votes.question: Kennedy Amdt. No. 6760 — To limit price increases for college athletics tickets.
votes.plain_language: This amendment would have barred colleges, conferences, and athletic associations from raising ticket prices for a sport by more than 4 percent from the prior academic year. A Yea would have added that cap. A Nay rejected it.

votes.question: Paul Amdt. No. 6758 — To improve the bill.
votes.plain_language: This amendment would have replaced the college-sports bill with the Collegiate Sports Integrity Act, which centers on an antitrust exemption for athletic conferences and associations. A Yea would have made that swap. A Nay rejected it.

votes.question: Baldwin Amdt. No. 6828 — To modify the provision relating to the relationship of this Act to existing law.
votes.plain_language: This amendment rewrites the college-sports bill's preemption section so states generally cannot set conflicting rules on athlete publicity pay, transfers, or certain eligibility, while keeping state civil-rights, contract, privacy, and similar laws unless they conflict. A Yea adopts that text. A Nay rejects it.

votes.question: H. Con. Res. 89 — A concurrent resolution directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran.
votes.plain_language: This House resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress has declared war or authorized that force, while still allowing defense against an imminent attack. A Yea would agree to that direction. A Nay rejects the resolution.

votes.bill_title: A concurrent resolution setting forth the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2026 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2027 through 2035.
votes.plain_language: This concurrent resolution establishes the congressional budget for the federal government for FY2026, sets forth budgetary levels for FY2027-FY2035, and provides reconciliation instructions for legislation that increases the deficit. A Yea agrees to it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: Schiff Amdt. No. 5333
votes.bill_title: A concurrent resolution setting forth the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2026 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2027 through 2035.
votes.plain_language: The sponsor's official statement of purpose for this amendment to S.Con.Res. 33 reads: “To establish a deficit-neutral reserve fund relating to requiring the obligation of amounts appropriated to the Federal Emergency Management Agency to carry out the public assistance and hazard mitigation programs.” A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: Wyden Amdt. No. 5336
votes.bill_title: A concurrent resolution setting forth the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2026 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2027 through 2035.
votes.plain_language: The sponsor's official statement of purpose for this amendment to S.Con.Res. 33 reads: “To establish a deficit-neutral reserve fund relating to requiring the Comptroller General of the United States to conduct a study related to economic consequences of private or confidential drug pricing agreements struck by any Federal department, agency, or office with any pharmaceutical manufacturer.” A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: Merkley Amdt. No. 5235
votes.bill_title: A concurrent resolution setting forth the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2026 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2027 through 2035.
votes.plain_language: The sponsor's official statement of purpose for this amendment to S.Con.Res. 33 reads: “To establish a deficit-neutral reserve fund relating to the impacts of hedge fund ownership of single-family homes and rent prices.” A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: Paul Amdt. No. 5378
votes.bill_title: A concurrent resolution setting forth the congressional budget for the United States Government for fiscal year 2026 and setting forth the appropriate budgetary levels for fiscal years 2027 through 2035.
votes.plain_language: The sponsor's official statement of purpose for this amendment to S.Con.Res. 33 reads: “To reduce new budget authority for functions 150, 250, 500, and 600 in order to offset $70,000,000,000 of new spending by cutting $45,000,000,000 of foreign aid, eliminating $5,000,000,000 in refugee spending, cutting $16,000,000,000 from the Department of Education, and cutting $4,000,000,000 of National Science Foundation funding.” A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: Motion to Waive All Applicable Budgetary Discipline Re: Markey Amdt. No. 5001

Today I joined the community of Hazen in dedicating a sculpture of the US Air Force’s SR-71  Blackbird and Hazen’s very own exceptional patriot, Major General Eldon Joersz. 
 
For nearly 24 years the iconic SR-71 operated as a strategic reconnaissance plane flying strategic missions from 1966 to 1990. Fifty years ago, Major General Eldon Joersz made history by becoming the fastest flying man alive when he flew the SR-71 over three times the speed of sound, reaching  a record breaking 2,193.176 mph. A record that still stands! 
 
“Today was not just about marking history. It's not just about pride. It is about imagining the future. It’s also about these young people who are here, that never know what it is to have had to go to war. But now they'll be able to come here, see this monument, and understand the cost of it.”
 
As Americans, let us embrace this bold and adventurous spirit, pushing past existing limits to redefine what is truly possible. Retired Major General Eldon Joersz, we thank you for your exceptional service to our country! Please accept the thanks of North Dakota.

Fascinating tour at @NDSU Biotech Innovation Core seeing innovation in action. Scott’s from Rolla and Kaycie is from West Fargo. They, along with the students and businesses they work with, are building on North Dakota’s world-class health and agriculture ecosystem. These homegrown solutions are what our state, nation, and the world needs.

Big things are happening in medical discovery here in North Dakota, and this innovative ecosystem has always been here, from our Norwegian ancestors to today. This has always been a place where people take an idea, put in hard work, apply intellectual rigor, and turn it into something that makes a difference. North Dakota, and especially the Fargo region, has what it takes—the talent, tools, and drive—to advance the bioscience sector and be part of the solution. I love how we don’t need to ask, “Why not in North Dakota?” because our people are already answering the question.
